lines.text: Morning, Kessel Patrol. Forty centimetres up high overnight. There is a call on your mission table.
Koda is already at the door.
Nobody flies in this. Wait for it to pass.
Data coming through. Nice work.
Pass road closed below Kessel Bowl.
Pass road open again.
The Grauhorn weather station stopped transmitting overnight.
Station is transmitting again. Thanks. Fresh numbers: forty centimetres overnight up there.
A van has slid into a drift on the Tannberg road.
Van is back on the road. The driver waved. Mostly.
Heavy loading reported above the pass road. Recon flight requested.
Report filed. Slopes A and C are loaded. We bring them down tomorrow, or today if you are up for it.
Slopes A and C above the pass road are ready to go. Bring them down on our terms.
Clean release, the berm held, the road is open. That is how it is done.
Charges set. Get clear of the slope: up on the ridge is safe. Then fire.
Fire in the hole.
Secondary release on the next slope over. That is fine, let it run.
It is down. A little over the road, but the barrier did its job.
It is down. The berm caught the lot. Beautiful.
New snow on Kessel Bowl and the wind has been at it. Which slopes are loaded today?
Report filed. The loaded slopes are flagged for the control team.
Kessel Bowl is loaded above the pass road. Bring it down before it comes down on its own.
Bowl is down and the road is open again. Good work up there.
Charge the slopes you think are loaded, then get clear and fire.
A skier missed the last chair. Last seen at the top station heading for the trees.
The clinic in Hollin is expecting him.
Nils is warm, splinted and eating soup. He says Koda is the best dog he has ever met.
A spruce has come down across the pass road below Kessel Bowl.
Pass road clear. Thanks for the quick work.
Kessel Patrol, it's Greta at the Kettle. I'm down to my last logs and there's snow on the way.
Oh, bless you both. Mind the step, it's icy.
That's the stove sorted for a week. Come in for a hot chocolate any time.
It's Greta again. Pepper went out before the snow and she hasn't come home.
Pepper! You silly thing. Come here, you are frozen.
Pepper is on the windowsill pretending none of this happened.
I heard the dog first. I thought I was dreaming.
Thank you. I really didn't fancy another night out here.
That's it, she's free! Thank you. I'd still be sat here at midnight.
